adversarialFindings.severity: HIGH -- it decides whether the Phase 0 exit can close at all
adversarialFindings.finding: The Phase 0 exit's ledger leg ACCEPTS ONLY 'excluded' for an out-of-scope county-scoped rail, so after P-252's scheduler flips those verdicts to 'refuse', six-county-completeness.mjs will report INCOMPLETE on maxImperviousCoverPct in all five non-Travis counties -- even though P-292 has removed the PUBLISH consequence.
adversarialFindings.fileAndLines: doc_repo scripts/six-county-completeness.mjs:52 (RAIL_POLICY: maxImperviousCoverPct { cls: 'county-scoped', accept: ['excluded'], onlyIn: ['48453'], ruling: 'engine #444' }) and :143-148 (the accept test: `const scopedOk = pol.cls !== 'county-scoped' || !pol.onlyIn.includes(fips); if (pol.accept?.includes(r.verdict) && scopedOk) { accepted } else { open }`).
adversarialFindings.why: Outside 48453, scopedOk is true and the only accepted verdict is 'excluded'. P-252 rewrites that row to 'refuse' (A-186's dry run measured 25 such verdicts, this rail among them). 'refuse' is not in accept, so the rail lands in `open` as { cls: 'county-scoped', verdict: 'refuse' } and the county reads INCOMPLETE. P-292 deliberately does NOT rewrite the verdict (that would fabricate an absence), so the two instruments now disagree about the same fact: the publish gate says 'not on this county's floor', the exit says 'incomplete'.
adversarialFindings.proposedAmendmentNotTakenHere: six-county-completeness.mjs:52 accept: ['excluded', 'refuse'] with a comment naming P-292/P-252 ('outside its scope the rail's honest verdict is refuse, never rewritten'), keeping the existing county-scoped-breach check at :138-141 that still flags a 'pass' outside onlyIn. That is a doc_repo edit, and doc_repo edits are planner-owned and six-county-completeness.mjs is P-253's repair, so this lane does NOT make it -- it is reported instead, with the line numbers, for the planner to route.

adversarialFindings.finding: The map is hand-declared, so a future change to the writer's county scope without a corresponding change to the map would leave the rail skipped in a county the writer now fills. The skip would then hide a live rail.
adversarialFindings.handling: (a) widening the map requires the county to be named in the entry's own ruling, refused at module load otherwise; (b) a test pins the map to exactly one entry with counties exactly ['48453'] and asserts the writer's own TRAVIS_FIPS and RAIL_KEY agree with it; (c) a test pins the drift-visible behaviour -- if an out-of-scope county's scoped rail ever reads 'pass', the skip still applies but carries verdict 'pass' in the record, which is the signal that the two have drifted. This is the map's named bypass rather than an unstated one.

adversarialFindings.finding: A syntactically valid but wrong FIPS in the map (a typo like 48435) would silently scope the rail to a county outside the program, skipping it everywhere.
adversarialFindings.handling: The load-time guard checks FIPS FORMAT only, which is honest about what it can know. The concrete protection is the exact-equality test on the shipped entry plus the ruling-names-the-county invariant, and the writer-agreement test. Stated as residual rather than claimed closed.
